name: Hur
overview: Hur was a male member of the tribe of Judah known for his significant role in supporting Moses during the battle against Amalek at Rephidim. He is specifically noted for holding up Moses' hands, an act that contributed to Israel's victory in this conflict. This role highlights his support and strength in a critical moment for the Israelites.
namesAndTitles: The name Hur appears as a proper name and is possibly understood to mean 'child.' There is no indication that this name was given by God, and it is simply recorded as Hur in Scripture.
familyAndRelationships: Hur is identified as a descendant of Judah, with inferred familial ties including Uri as his father and Chelubai as his son. Additional inferred relationships include Shobal, Salma, Hareph, Penuel, and Ezer as his descendants, indicating a notable lineage within the tribe of Judah.
scriptureSignificance: Hur's importance in the biblical narrative lies in his practical support of Moses during a pivotal battle, symbolizing faithful assistance in God's deliverance of Israel. By holding up Moses' hands, Hur enabled the Israelites to prevail over Amalek, demonstrating the power of perseverance and cooperation under God's guidance. His involvement underscores the role of faithful leadership and support in fulfilling God's purposes for His people.
